# On-demand SDK regeneration (rwx run .rwx/regenerate.yml). Unlike
# spec-update-check.yml there is no drift check or issue handling: it
# regenerates from the spec already committed (or, with --init fetch=true,
# the latest upstream spec), runs mypy and pytest, and emits a
# patch artifact. It never commits, pushes, or opens a PR. Use it for
# regeneration work such as #57.
#
# Required secret: SPEAKEASY_API_KEY in the sdk-python-attio vault. No GitHub write token is used.
on:
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      fetch: "false"
  # `rwx dispatch regenerate --ref main` runs from main, the only ref the
  # sdk-python-attio vault releases SPEAKEASY_API_KEY to. Pass
  # `--param fetch=true` to adopt the latest upstream spec.
  dispatch:
    - key: regenerate
      title: Regenerate SDK
      params:
        - key: fetch
          description: Adopt the latest upstream spec before generating.
          default: "false"
          values: ["false", "true"]
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        fetch: ${{ event.dispatch.params.fetch }}

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

concurrency-pools:
  - id: elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio:regenerate
    capacity: 1
    on-overflow: queue

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      preserve-git-dir: true
      fetch-full-depth: true

  - key: python
    call: python/install 2.0.1
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"

  - key: uv
    use: python
    run: pip install uv

  - key: sync
    use: [code, uv]
    run: uv sync
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock

  # Snapshot the tree before generation. The patch is diffed against this
  # snapshot, so local changes `rwx run` uploads on top of the commit are
  # not mistaken for generation output.
  - key: baseline
    use: sync
    run: |
      git add -A
      git write-tree > .git/regen-base-tree

  # Same pinned, checksum-verified installer as spec-update-check.yml. This
  # task never sees SPEAKEASY_API_KEY.
  - key: speakeasy-cli
    use: baseline
    run: |
      curl -fsSL -o /tmp/speakeasy-install.sh \
        https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speakeasy-api/speakeasy/89688fa0cfc3c959f4ac370329325d1b274db551/install.sh
      echo "9e2c4f1054e214d05352597cfd9ed1ab117a089e9442f532dd4a0d168665d757  /tmp/speakeasy-install.sh" \
        | sha256sum -c -
      VERSION=1.804.0 sh /tmp/speakeasy-install.sh

  # Uncached: the output depends on the Speakeasy service and the key, not
  # only on repo content.
  - key: generate
    use: speakeasy-cli
    cache: false
    timeout: 60m
    env:
      SPEAKEASY_API_KEY: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-attio.secrets.SPEAKEASY_API_KEY }}
      SPEAKEASY_USE_HOST_CLI: "1"
      SPEAKEASY_FAIL_ON_VERSION_MISMATCH: "true"
      FETCH: ${{ init.fetch }}
    run: |
      # --no-fetch regenerates from the committed spec; fetch=true adopts the
      # latest upstream spec first. generate refuses to run on an unhealthy
      # overlay (_verify_overlay_health); do not bypass it.
      if [ "$FETCH" = "true" ]; then
        uv run python ci/pipeline.py generate
      else
        uv run python ci/pipeline.py generate --no-fetch
      fi

  - key: verify
    use: generate
    # A timeout SIGKILLs the task and skips patch, so no artifact is produced;
    # the 10m default is too short for mypy plus the full test suite.
    timeout: 60m
    run: |
      uv lock
      uv sync
      uv run python ci/spec_diff.py check-overlay
      uv run mypy generated/src
      uv run pytest -q

  # Regeneration only produces a patch; nothing is committed or pushed. Apply
  # it locally:
  #   rwx artifacts download <run-id> --task patch regenerate-patch --auto-extract
  #   git apply .rwx/downloads/<dir>/regenerate.patch
  - key: patch
    use: verify
    run: |
      base=$(cat .git/regen-base-tree)
      allow="generated openapi .speakeasy pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md"
      # Anything generation changed outside the allowlist means a step leaked.
      leftovers=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } \
        | grep -v '^tmp/' \
        | grep -vE '^(generated|openapi|\.speakeasy)/|^(pyproject\.toml|uv\.lock|README\.md)$' || true)
      if [ -n "$leftovers" ]; then
        echo "Unexpected changes outside the regeneration allowlist ($allow):" >&2
        echo "$leftovers" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # -N records new files in the diff.
      git add -N $allow
      git diff --binary "$base" -- $allow > regenerate.patch
      [ -s regenerate.patch ] || echo "Regeneration produced no changes."
      git diff --stat "$base" -- $allow
    outputs:
      artifacts:
        - key: regenerate-patch
          path: regenerate.patch

# Weekly drift detection against https://api.attio.com/openapi/api.
# Replaces the GitHub Actions spec-update-check.yml.
#
#   check       -> ci/pipeline.py check-openapi (never fails the task; the
#                  verdict is written to values so notify can always run)
#   regenerate  -> when the spec drifted, the overlay is healthy, and
#                  SPEAKEASY_API_KEY exists: adopt the spec, regenerate, run
#                  pytest, open a PR from an agent/spec-update-* branch.
#                  Always runs; writes a `result` value (success|failure|skipped).
#   notify      -> opens/updates/closes the "needs attention" issue.
#   verdict     -> fails the run if check or regenerate failed.
#
# Required vault secrets: GITHUB_TOKEN (contents+pull-requests+issues write;
# the repo is public, so cloning needs no token),
# SPEAKEASY_API_KEY, read from the sdk-python-attio vault (optional; without
# it, drift only produces an issue. The vault is locked to main, so a CLI
# run from another ref fails at secret resolution before any task runs).
# No task pushes to main.
on:
  cron:
    - key: weekly-spec-check
      schedule: "0 9 * * MON"
      init:
        # Cron events carry no commit SHA; the schedule runs on main.
        commit-sha: main
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}

version: 2

on:
  github:
    push:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
      if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
    # PR runs reach the vault unattended, but only for PRs authored by the
    # repo owner: the `if:` below is the author gate (vault grants match only
    # repo + branch pattern, never author). See the integration-tests task.
    pull_request:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: pull_request
      if: ${{ event.github.pull_request.pull_request.user.login == 'elviskahoro' }}
  cron:
    - key: weekly-integration-tests
      schedule: 17 7 * * 1
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
  cli:
    # Manual `rwx run` dispatch; the account user holds vault access.
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: ${{ init.repository }}
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

  # No packaged `uv/install` leaf exists in the RWX catalog (verified via
  # `rwx packages list` 2026-10-03 -- `python/install` installs Python, not
  # uv), so this manual installer stays. Checksum-pinned so an altered or
  # compromised script at that URL fails closed instead of executing -- same
  # pattern as gtm-sdk's .rwx/lint.yml uv-install task.
  # The source workflow's astral-sh/setup-uv resolved the latest uv (it pins
  # only the action, not uv); this port pins 0.11.29 instead -- the version
  # the exact steps below were validated against (uv sync --locked + full
  # pytest suite). Unlike gtm-sdk, this repo's pyproject.toml carries no
  # [tool.uv] required-version pin, so bumping this is safe as long as the
  # committed uv.lock still parses and `uv sync --locked` stays clean.
  - key: uv-install
    use: [code]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # No `filter:` here -- `uv sync` installs gtm-linear editable and the test
  # suite imports scripts/ and operations/ too, so the full source tree must
  # be present (same rationale as gtm-sdk's .rwx/lint.yml deps task).
  # UV_LOCKED and UV_PYTHON are exported to $RWX_ENV so every downstream
  # `uv run` inherits them -- the RWX equivalent of the source workflow's
  # workflow-level `env:` block, which existed so `uv run` steps fail loudly
  # on lockfile drift instead of silently re-resolving off PyPI. UV_PYTHON
  # mirrors setup-uv's python-version input (which sets UV_PYTHON).
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_LOCKED: "1"
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      uv sync
      echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      echo "$PWD/.venv" > "$RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV"
      echo "1" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_LOCKED"
      echo "3.13" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_PYTHON"

  - key: captain
    call: rwx/install-captain 1.2.0

  # The live-API half of the network suite: the CLI live wording check plus
  # the tests/integration suite, with LINEAR_API_KEY from the
  # `sdk-python-linear-it` vault.
  #
  # That vault is deliberately NOT the `sdk-python-linear` one the other
  # pipelines use. It holds exactly one secret -- a key for a disposable
  # Linear workspace we accept may leak -- because PR runs reach it with no
  # approval, and a PR can edit this file to exfiltrate whatever the vault
  # holds. `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `PYPI_TOKEN` stay in the main-only vault.
  # Never add another secret to `sdk-python-linear-it`.
  #
  # Access model (`rwx vaults show sdk-python-linear-it`): locked, repository
  # grants `elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear:**`, `:*/*` and `:main`, approvals
  # disabled. Branch patterns do not cross `/` (not even `**`): `*/*` is what
  # matches one-segment-prefixed branches like `w-565/...`.
  # A same-repo ref matching a grant resolves the key unattended (names with
  # two or more `/` do not). Approvals must stay off:
  # a ref matching no grant fails before `run:` when approvals are disabled,
  # which is why `**` is granted rather than relying on approval to pause.
  # The only author gate is the `pull_request` trigger's `if:` above; a branch
  # pushed by another collaborator is not covered by it.
  #
  # Vault matching uses the run's own repository/ref context from the trigger
  # event, NOT `init` parameters (#163 tried `branch:` in the init and
  # reverted). The vault's "Allow public repositories" toggle is UI-only and
  # invisible to `rwx vaults show`; keep it set.
  #
  # cache: false mirrors schema-drift (the result depends on Linear's live
  # API, not just repo files); cache-key: excluded keeps the credential out
  # of the task's content-cache fingerprint.
  - key: integration-tests
    use: [deps, captain]
    cache: false
    env:
      LINEAR_API_KEY:
        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-linear-it.secrets.LINEAR_API_KEY }}
        cache-key: excluded
    run: captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest-integration

  - key: dagger-install
    use: [uv-install]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64)
          asset=dagger_v0.21.11_linux_amd64.tar.gz
          sha256=a2d3ef96e7305abc18663a3606d9c1c592278ba3c8f48e01d6be14eef72276ef

          ;;
        *)
          echo "unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2
          exit 1
          ;;
      esac
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
      curl -fsSL "https://dl.dagger.io/dagger/releases/0.21.11/${asset}" -o "${tmp}/dagger.tgz"
      echo "${sha256}  ${tmp}/dagger.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
      mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
      tar -xzf "${tmp}/dagger.tgz" -C "$HOME/.local/bin" dagger
      dagger version

  # Offline guard confirms the active SHA matches Renovate's metadata record;
  # it does not verify that the SHA belongs to the recorded release tag.
  # Weekly RWX verifies that mapping and reports drift, but does not block publishing.
  - key: verify-pin
    use: [dagger-install]
    run: bash scripts/dagger_ref_drift.sh --verify-pin

  - key: build
    use: [verify-pin]
    run: |
      # Required format: publisher-module-sha: <tag> <40-character lowercase SHA>.
      # Keep this record within 8 lines of the dagger -m command for Renovate.
      # publisher-module-sha: v0.2.2 1cdcc45e2e4fe78768d73def9cbe23a54209f618
      dagger -m github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-publish-to-pypi@1cdcc45e2e4fe78768d73def9cbe23a54209f618 call build --source . export --path dist

  # PyPI trusted publishing is GitHub-OIDC-bound, so RWX publishes with a
  # project-scoped API token from the repo-scoped vault. Provision with:
  #   rwx vaults secrets set --vault sdk-python-linear PYPI_TOKEN=<token>
  # cache: false so a publish is never skipped by a cache hit.
  - key: publish
    use: [build]
    cache: false
    env:
      UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN:
        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-linear.secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
        cache-key: excluded
    run: uv publish dist/*

tasks:

      # Shallow clone (git/clone's default) is enough: the check reads the

  # `filter: []` and no TTL, so by default this task would be cached
  # indefinitely on whatever gh version the first run installed -- RWX's
  # caching docs call out exactly this "install latest" hazard

  # command tasks (not `call`), so this opts out of caching entirely; at this

  - key: gh-install

## Development Setup

1. Fork and clone the repository.
2. Install dependencies using `uv` (recommended) or `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
3. Run the development server: `reflex run`.

## Frontend dependency security fixes

Reflex 0.10.0 restores `reflex.lock/package.json` and `reflex.lock/bun.lock`
when generating `.web`. Keep both files committed together. Put transitive
security pins in the persisted manifest's `overrides`, then let Bun generate
the matching lockfile:

```sh
cd reflex.lock
bun install --lockfile-only
bun audit
```

Use Bun 1.4 or newer, which supports this lockfile format. To verify a fresh
frontend generation and production build, run from the repository root:

```sh
REFLEX_WEB_WORKDIR=.web-security-check uv run reflex export --frontend-only --no-zip
cd .web-security-check
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun audit
```

Remove `.web-security-check` after verification. Preserve the security overrides
when updating dependencies: the current pins patch KaTeX, postcss-selector-parser,
socket.io-parser, source-map-js, and ws. KaTeX, postcss-selector-parser, and ws
exceed their parents' declared version ranges; check Markdown math rendering,
Tailwind typography output, and WebSocket connections when changing those
overrides. Reassess the pins when their parent packages support patched versions
directly.

### Known advisories pinned by Reflex 0.10.0

The following advisories are pinned by upstream Reflex 0.10.0 dependencies and
cannot be upgraded without a Reflex version bump:

- **vite 8.3.2**: Multiple moderate to high severity advisories (cross-origin script
  execution, file serving restrictions, editor flag misinterpretation). Reflex 0.10.0
  pins vite via @react-router/dev.
- **KaTeX, postcss-selector-parser**: Patched via security overrides in the
  manifest's `overrides` section.

## Adding Components

- New components should be added to `app/base_ui/components/base/`.
- Use `CoreComponent` or `BaseUIComponent` as base classes to ensure theme compatibility.
- Use `oklch` CSS variables for all colors.

## Adding Examples

- Add your example card to `app/examples/components.py`.
- Use the `@masonry_card(label="Category")` decorator.
- Categories include: `General`, `Finance`, `Healthcare`, `Tech`, `Government`.

## Coding Standards

- Follow PEP 8 for Python code.
- Ensure all components are accessible (ARIA roles, keyboard support).
- Use `rx.cond` and `rx.match` for dynamic, client-side logic where possible.

## Pull Requests

- Create a feature branch for your changes.
- Provide a clear description of the problem solved or the feature added.
- Include a screenshot or recording of new UI components.

Thank you for helping make Buridan UI the standard for Reflex applications!

- Failed or PENDING_FAILURE: PENDING_FAILURE may be a flake, so retry once.
  Failed means push a fix to the PR branch and resubmit. Do not resubmit
  blindly in a loop.
- Auth failure: run `trunk login` once and retry.
- Refuse to queue from main or a protected branch.
- A `Closes #N` line in the PR body auto-closes the issue when the queue lands
  the PR. Do not close the issue by hand beforehand.

Because the queue auto-merges once its predictive CI passes, the user's "yes"
on the final PR preview is the explicit human authorization to merge — after
it, submit with `trunk merge <pr-number>` without re-prompting. There is no
second gate before the merge lands.

The queue's required statuses live in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`
(`merge.required_statuses`) and must be live GitHub check names posted on
every PR. Re-verify after any pipeline rename:
`gh pr checks <pr-number> --json name --jq '.[].name'`. Do not add
path-filtered or `workflow_run`-triggered workflows there: they do not report
on every PR and would deadlock the queue.

Graph mode adds one more admission gate beyond `merge.required_statuses`: the
queue holds every PR at Not Ready until impacted targets have been uploaded
for its head sha. `.github/workflows/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` uploads them
on every PR to main (`PUT /v2/impacted-targets` authorized by the
`TRUNK_API_TOKEN` repo secret). The job stays out of
`merge.required_statuses` on purpose — the queue waits on the upload itself,
not the check — but a red `Upload Impacted Targets` job means nothing was
uploaded, and PRs stall at Not Ready even with every required status green.

`pullfrog-approval` (Pullfrog's AI review verdict) is required on the GitHub
side only (ruleset `main - PR requirements` plus classic branch protection on
`main`, pinned to the Pullfrog app). It is deliberately not in
`merge.required_statuses`, so the Trunk queue does not wait on it.

This is the CI/CD inventory for buridan-ui, plus the RWX reference pattern from `sdk-python-attio` and `sdk-python-linear`. Nothing was modified. The sibling `.rwx/*.yml` files are quoted verbatim below. Four of them (`spec-update-check.yml`, the Linear `dagger-ref-drift.yml`, the Linear `.migration-inventory.md` and the Linear `publish.yml` header) were not fully read, and I did not open the 11 non-`.rwx` references in the Attio and Linear trunk and `AGENTS.md` files.

## 1. buridan-ui: current CI/CD state

**Branch and RWX status.**
- The checked-out branch is `conductor/rwx-ci-cd-migration`. It sits at `ebce196`, which is also `origin/main`. It has no commits of its own and a clean tree, so no migration work has started.
- There is no `.rwx/` directory and no RWX reference anywhere in the working tree.
- `git grep -i rwx` on HEAD finds only `reflex.lock/bun.lock`, which is an unrelated hash match. The only RWX mention is in `.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`: "gtm-sdk's lint pipeline does the same (its .rwx/trunk-check.yml deps task runs uv sync before checks)".
- Git history has no `.rwx` files. The `-S'.rwx'` hits are `10bbb3d`, `ea7f891` and `b1cbb69`, the "Trunk Merge Queue setup (#124)" commits, which carry that same comment line.
- Relevant history:
  - `10bbb3d` (#124) added the trunk merge-queue CI gates.
  - `71dbe68` (#230) added the impacted-targets upload.
  - `e98abdf` (#232) switched Pullfrog to glm-5p3-flash.
  - `8ae83f8` (#59) and `6f52201` (#46) set up Pullfrog.
  - `9a4abb1` (#84) added the docs-and-assets validation workflow.
  - Older commits ("update deploy github workflow", `e0b2329`, `ac24fb3`, `265182d`) show a former deploy workflow that no longer exists.
- Local `main` (`5c89bf2`) is stale relative to `origin/main`. `git rev-parse` also printed a promisor/corruption warning about `ebce196` being missing from the object store. Treat `git diff main` as unreliable and compare against `origin/main`.

**Absent entirely:**
- `.github/actions`
- dependabot or renovate config
- Makefile
- Dockerfile
- `vercel.json`
- `.pre-commit-config`
- any Reflex Cloud or Vercel deploy config

`.github/FUNDING.yml` only holds `github: [LineIndent]`. `rxconfig.py` is app config only and has no deploy block. `reflex-hosting-cli` is a dev dependency, but nothing invokes it. The old deploy workflow is gone.

### Workflows (`/home/vercel-sandbox/buridan-ui/.github/workflows/`)

All five declare `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level.

**1. `tests.yml` (workflow "Tests", job `tests`, check name "Tests")**
- Triggers: `push` on `main` and `trunk-merge/**`, and `pull_request` on `main`.
- Runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Steps:
  1. `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5… # v7.0.1`
  2. `astral-sh/setup-uv@1c37ad07… # v10.3.0` (caching on by default)
  3. `uv sync --frozen --group dev`
  4. `uv run pytest -q`
- It uses no secrets or env.

**2. `trunk-check.yml` (workflow "Trunk Check", job `trunk-check`, check name "Trunk Check")**
- Triggers: `push` on `trunk-merge/**` only, and `pull_request` on `main`. There is deliberately no push-to-main run.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout with `fetch-depth: 0`.
  2. `setup-uv`, then `uv sync --frozen --group dev`. This is needed because pyrefly and pyright resolve against `.venv`.
  3. Install the trunk launcher, checksum-pinned. It runs `curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk`, verifies `sha256 700f8bbe…f322`, then runs `sudo install -m 755 … /usr/local/bin/trunk`.
  4. For `pull_request` events:
     - If `GITHUB_REF == refs/pull/$PR_NUMBER/merge`, set `upstream=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)`.
     - Otherwise set `upstream=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`.
     - Then run `trunk check --upstream="$upstream" --ci < /dev/null`.
  5. For `push` events: `trunk check --upstream="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)" --ci < /dev/null`.
- Env: `PR_NUMBER` comes from `github.event.pull_request.number`. No secrets.

**3. `validate-assets.yml` (workflow "Docs & Assets", job `validate-generated-assets`, check name "Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards")**
- Triggers: `push` on `main` and `trunk-merge/**`, and `pull_request` on `main`.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout `3d3c42e5… v7.0.1`.
  2. `actions/setup-python@5fda3b95… v7.0.0` with Python 3.12.
  3. `pip install uv`
  4. `uv sync --group dev` (not `--frozen`)
  5. `uv run python scripts/generate_anatomy.py --check`
  6. `uv run python scripts/generate_markdown.py`
  7. `git diff --exit-code assets/docs`
  8. `uv run pytest tests/test_generated_assets.py tests/test_toc_scrollspy.py`
- No secrets.

**4. `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` (workflow "Trunk Impacted Targets", job `upload-impacted-targets`, "Upload Impacted Targets")**
- Trigger: `pull_request` on `main`, with no path filters. A comment forbids adding any.
- One step, a shell `curl`:
  - It does `PUT https://api.trunk.io/v2/impacted-targets` with a JSON body of `repositoryId`, `targetBranch`, `sha`, `number` and `impactsAllTargets:true`.
  - It exits 0 with a warning if the token is empty (fork or Dependabot PRs), and fails unless the response is HTTP 202.
- Secret: `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` (`secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN`).
- Env: `TRUNK_REPOSITORY_ID=c064fac2-557f-48fd-9979-1f94fa82cb55`, `PR_NUMBER`, `HEAD_SHA`, `TARGET_BRANCH`.
- It is deliberately not in `required_statuses`, but a red run stalls the queue at "Not Ready".

**5. `pullfrog.yml` (workflow "Pullfrog")**
- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only, with inputs `prompt` and `name`. The header says it is vendor-managed: "DO NOT EDIT EXCEPT WHERE INDICATED".
- Permissions are `id-token: write` and `contents: read`.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout `d23441a4… v6.1.0` with `fetch-depth: 1`.
  2. `pullfrog/pullfrog@ad4283a8… v0.1.98` with `model: fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash`.
- Secrets passed as env: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. Bedrock, Vertex, Azure and OpenAI-compatible variables are commented out.
- `.trunk/trunk.yaml` has a checkov ignore for this file.

### Trunk and merge queue (`.trunk/trunk.yaml`)
- CLI version 1.25.0. Plugin sources: trunk `v1.11.0`, `oss-linter-trunk` `v0.2026.04.14.00.00`, add-trailing-comma `v0.1.0`, pyrefly-plugin `v0.2.1`, tach-plugin `v0.1.0`.
- It overrides the actionlint download URL to the `kjanat/actionlint` fork.
- It overrides pyright to use `${workspace}/.venv/bin/python`. It scopes vale to `docs/**/*.md(x)`.
- It enables linters including actionlint, bandit, checkov, osv-scanner, pinact, pyrefly, pyright, ruff, semgrep, shellcheck, tach, trivy, trufflehog, ty, vale, yamlfmt and yamllint.
- Actions: `trunk-cache-prune` and `trunk-upgrade-available` are enabled. The git-hook actions are disabled so Entire can own `core.hooksPath`.
- `merge.required_statuses` is currently:
  - `Trunk Check`
  - `Tests`
  - `Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards`
- `pullfrog-approval` is required only through the GitHub ruleset "main - PR requirements" and classic branch protection. It is deliberately not in the trunk list.
- The comment block says never to add path-filtered or `workflow_run` workflows, because they would deadlock the queue.
- Other files in `.trunk/`: `.gitignore` and `configs/{.isort.cfg,.yamllint.yaml,.markdownlint.yaml,ruff.toml}`.

### Other CI-adjacent files
- Docs: `AGENTS.md` lines 25–60 describe the queue, the `trunk merge <pr>` flow and the `required_statuses` rules. `CLAUDE.md` is a stub that points at `.entire/agent-guide.md`.
- Scripts CI calls: `scripts/generate_anatomy.py` (`--check`), `scripts/generate_markdown.py`, `tests/test_generated_assets.py` and `tests/test_toc_scrollspy.py`. The rest of `scripts/` is `generate_{llms,preview_cards,registry,search_index,sitemap}.py`, `linear_cli.py` and `run_all.py`.
- Python is pinned in `.python-version`. `pyproject.toml` has `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days"`, `prerelease = "allow"`, and a dev group with `reflex==0.10.0`, `pytest>=9.1.1` and others.
- Agent and tooling config:
  - `.roborev.toml`: agent `pi`, model `fireworks/…/glm-5p3-flash`.
  - `.conductor/settings.toml`: PR prompts only.
  - `.claude/settings.json`: Entire hooks.
  - `.entire/`
  - `.pi/extensions/entire`
  - `.vale.ini`, `tach.toml`, `pyrefly.toml`, `pyrightconfig.json`, `configs/pyrightconfig.json`.
- Secrets in use across all workflows are `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` plus Pullfrog's provider keys.

## 2. RWX reference checkouts

Only `sdk-python-attio` and `sdk-python-linear` match the ask. Other `.rwx/` dirs exist in `gtm-sdk`, `wedding`, `flox-conductor-sandbox` and `reflex-starter-template`. The comments in both sibling repos name `gtm-sdk` as the original pilot, so it is the best source for a queue-gated pipeline.

### How GitHub workflows were handled
- **sdk-python-linear**
  - Commit `00e2f2a` (#60) deleted `ci.yml` and `dagger-ref-drift.yml` after the RWX ports were validated through live dispatches. It also updated the inventory, README and CHANGELOG.

```yaml
# Not path-filtered: a path-filtered required check does not report on
# every PR and would deadlock the Trunk Merge Queue. PR and queue/main pushes
# share one status-check name so a single check covers both.
on:
  github:
    pull_request:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        lint-upstream: origin/main
      status-checks:
        name: trunk-check
    push:
      - if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
          lint-upstream: HEAD^
        status-checks:
          name: trunk-check
      - if: ${{ starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/') || starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge-beta/') }}
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
          lint-upstream: origin/main
        status-checks:
          name: trunk-check
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      lint-upstream: origin/main

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      preserve-git-dir: true
      fetch-full-depth: true

  - key: python
    call: python/install 2.0.1
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"

  - key: uv
    use: python
    run: pip install uv

  - key: sync
    use: [code, uv]
    run: uv sync
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock

  # Trunk launcher, checksum-pinned: trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only,
  # so the bytes are pinned and any upstream change fails closed (same pin as
  # .rwx/pytest.yml). Re-pin deliberately if the checksum no longer matches.
  - key: trunk-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" /usr/local/bin/trunk 2>/dev/null; then
        mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
        install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" "$HOME/.local/bin/trunk"
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"

  # Tool cache. A `filter` scopes only the task that defines it: downstream
  # `use:`rs do NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file, so
  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config keys on .trunk/ alone, freezing the
  # $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes (outside-workspace files are always
  # keyed, never filtered); trunk-tools keys on .trunk/ plus the pinned
  # launcher. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin is downloaded once and
  # reused until trunk.yaml changes. Keep the two filter lists in lockstep.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: code
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      cp -r .trunk "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk"
      rm -rf "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk/.gitignore"
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      git init -q
      # Pin the dates so a cold-cache re-execution writes identical bytes
      # instead of busting trunk-tools' key with wall-clock timestamps.
      export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      export GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      git -c user.name=rwx -c user.email=rwx@example.com commit -q --allow-empty -m seed

  - key: trunk-tools
    use: [trunk-install, trunk-config]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      trunk install --ci < /dev/null

  - key: lint
    use: [sync, trunk-tools]
    env:
      UPSTREAM: ${{ init.lint-upstream }}
    run: |
      # Lint only the diff, like trunk-action. The trigger picks the base
      # (PR/queue: main, push to main: previous commit) rather than this
      # script inferring it from the branch name, which a fork PR from its
      # own `main` would spoof.
      if [ "$UPSTREAM" = "origin/main" ]; then
        git fetch origin main
      fi
      trunk check --ci --upstream "$UPSTREAM"
```

```yaml
    with:

  - key: uv
    use: python
    run: pip install uv

  - key: sync
    use: [code, uv]
    run: uv sync

    # in the workspace or `import attio` fails on a fresh (uncached) sync.

      - uv.lock

  # JUnit files, and `pytest` re-fails on the saved code.

    # so a quarantine granted after the original run never applies.

      captain run sdk-python-attio-pytest

        cache-key: excluded

      TRUNK_ANALYTICS_CLI_VERSION: "0.16.1"
      CUSTOM: "true"

      PR_NUMBER: ${{ init.pr-number }}
      COMMIT_BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      COMMIT_SHA: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      REPO: ${{ init.repository }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      # RWX auto-exposes RWX_RUN_URL (www.rwx.com/docs/environment-variables).
      export JOB_URL="${RWX_RUN_URL}"
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then

        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2

      # carries the CLI's exit code through tee, the grep catches its error
      # banner under the quarantining exit code, and
      # --allow-empty-test-results=false catches a glob matching no files.
      # --pr-number is only valid when non-empty (push legs set it to "").

      # keep Trunk's history ordered; fall back if the checkout lacks it.
      commit_epoch="$(git show -s --format=%ct "${COMMIT_SHA}" 2>/dev/null || date +%s)"

        --junit-paths "tmp/junit-*.xml" \
        --allow-empty-test-results=false \
        --org-url-slug "${TRUNK_ORG_SLUG}" \
        --use-uncloned-repo \
        --repo-url "${REPO}" \
        --repo-head-sha "${COMMIT_SHA}" \
        --repo-head-branch "${BRANCH}" \
        --repo-head-author-name rwx \
        --repo-head-commit-epoch "${commit_epoch}" \
```

```yaml
base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:

    call: git/clone 2.2.0

      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

      # shallow snapshot (same reason gtm-sdk's trunk-check code task sets
      # these flags, unlike this repo's tests.yml clone, which nothing
      # history-dependent consumes). Public repo, so no github-token is
      # needed.

      preserve-git-dir: true

      script="$(mktemp)"

      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -

  # NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file

  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter, and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config's keys its own cache on .trunk/
  # alone, freezing the $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes for downstream keys
  # (outside-workspace files are always keyed, never filtered);
  # trunk-tools' scopes its key to .trunk/ plus the pinned launcher binary
  # trunk-install writes. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin in trunk.yaml

    use: [code]

      - .trunk/configs

      mkdir -p "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      cp -r .trunk "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk"
      rm -rf "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk/.gitignore"

    # filters apply only to the task defining them, so without this one
    # trunk-tools would key on the whole clone and cache-miss on every
    # commit. It needs nothing else from the workspace -- the seed repo and

      - .trunk/configs

      set -euo pipefail

      # to find the actual fork point (stable even when main has moved).

      # When main hasn't moved, merge-base equals BASE_SHA (identical behavior).
      # When main has moved, merge-base returns the actual fork point.
      MERGE_BASE="$(git merge-base HEAD "${BASE_SHA}")"
      trunk check --upstream="${MERGE_BASE}" --ci < /dev/null

  # Post-merge safety net (push to main, or manual `rwx run` dispatch): lint
  # the whole tree, not just a PR diff, so drift that slipped past incremental
  # PR runs turns main red.
  - key: trunk-check-full
    use: [trunk-tools, deps]
    if: ${{ init.event-type == 'push' }}
    run: trunk check --all --ci < /dev/null

  # Tach's external-dependency audit (the `unused_external_dependencies =
  # "error"` rule in tach.toml): fails if pyproject.toml declares a runtime
  # dependency no package file imports. Runs here as its own task because it
  # cannot be a Trunk lint command: Trunk executes batch lint commands from
  # a sandbox holding only the diff's files, and the audit decides "used"
  # from the imports visible there, so every dependency whose import sites
  # sit outside the diff got a false "not used" error (observed on #108's
  # own PR: all four runtime deps flagged, which would have rejected every
  # queue entry once the merge queue gates on the lint pipeline). Here it
  # sees the full checkout, like the drift checks in [test]. The tach pin in
  # pyproject.toml matches the trunk-managed tach@0.35.1 the module-boundary
  # lint gate uses.
  - key: tach-external
    use: [deps]
    run: uv run tach check-external
```

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      init:

        branch: ${{ event.git.branch }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: push
        pr-author: ""
        pr-number: ""
      if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
    pull_request:
      # The source GHA workflow (deleted in the flip) declared

      # no base-branch `if:` here -- unlike gtm-sdk's .rwx configs, whose
      # source gated on main.
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        branch: ${{ event.git.branch }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: pull_request
        pr-author: ${{ event.github.pull_request.pull_request.user.login }}
        pr-number: ${{ event.github.pull_request.pull_request.number }}
  cron:
    - key: weekly-schema-drift
      # Source workflow: `schedule: cron: 17 6 * * 1` -- weekly Monday 06:17
      # UTC (no timezone declared in the source cron, so UTC). Catches Linear
      # changing its schema out from under the pinned copy. Cron schedules run
      # against the default branch; event.git.* resolves in this trigger
      # context (same pattern as gtm-sdk's .rwx/tests-bazel-full.yml, whose
      # live cron runs confirmed it).
      schedule: 17 6 * * 1
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        branch: ${{ event.git.branch }}
        repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
        event-type: schedule
        pr-author: ""
        pr-number: ""
  cli:
    # Manual `rwx run` dispatch for validation -- the source workflow has no
    # workflow_dispatch. Mirrors the push trigger's init so a dispatch
    # exercises the push path. schema-drift runs on every trigger.
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      branch: ${{ event.git.branch }}
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear.git
      event-type: push
      pr-author: ""
      pr-number: ""

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: ${{ init.repository }}
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      # Source workflow used actions/checkout with its default fetch-depth: 1;
      # nothing in the test suite or the two --check scripts reads git
      # history, so git/clone's default shallow fetch matches. The repo is
      # public, so no github-token is needed (gtm-sdk's .rwx configs need one
      # only because that repo is private).

  # The publisher-drift integration test executes the same jq projection that
  # `gh issue list --jq` uses, including its base64/TSV handling of issue bodies.
  # Pin the release and checksum; install it into the shared tool path.
  - key: jq-install
    use: [code]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      tool_dir="$HOME/.local/bin"
      mkdir -p "$tool_dir"
      jq_path="$tool_dir/jq"
      case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64)
          jq_asset=jq-linux-amd64
          jq_sha256=5942c9b0934e510ee61eb3e30273f1b3fe2590df93933a93d7c58b81d19c8ff5
          ;;
        aarch64|arm64)
          jq_asset=jq-linux-arm64
          jq_sha256=4dd2d8a0661df0b22f1bb9a1f9830f06b6f3b8f7d91211a1ef5d7c4f06a8b4a5
          ;;
        *)
          echo "unsupported jq runner architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2
          exit 1
          ;;
      esac
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/${jq_asset}" -o "$jq_path"
      echo "${jq_sha256}  ${jq_path}" | sha256sum -c -
      chmod 0755 "$jq_path"
      "$jq_path" --version
      echo "$tool_dir" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # No packaged `uv/install` leaf exists in the RWX catalog (verified via
  # `rwx packages list` 2026-10-03 -- `python/install` installs Python, not
  # uv), so this manual installer stays. Checksum-pinned so an altered or
  # compromised script at that URL fails closed instead of executing -- same
  # pattern as gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml uv-install task.
  # The source workflow's astral-sh/setup-uv resolved the latest uv (it pins
  # only the action, not uv); this port pins 0.11.29 instead -- the version
  # the exact steps below were validated against (uv sync --locked + full
  # pytest suite). Unlike gtm-sdk, this repo's pyproject.toml carries no
  # [tool.uv] required-version pin, so bumping this is safe as long as the
  # committed uv.lock still parses and `uv sync --locked` stays clean.
  - key: uv-install
    use: [jq-install]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # No `filter:` here -- `uv sync` installs gtm-linear editable and the test
  # suite imports scripts/ and operations/ too, so the full source tree must
  # be present (same rationale as gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml deps task).
  # UV_LOCKED and UV_PYTHON are exported to $RWX_ENV so every downstream
  # `uv run` inherits them -- the RWX equivalent of the source workflow's
  # workflow-level `env:` block, which existed so `uv run` steps fail loudly
  # on lockfile drift instead of silently re-resolving off PyPI. UV_PYTHON
  # mirrors setup-uv's python-version input (which sets UV_PYTHON).
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_LOCKED: "1"
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      uv sync
      echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      echo "$PWD/.venv" > "$RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV"
      echo "1" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_LOCKED"
      echo "3.13" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_PYTHON"

  - key: captain
    call: rwx/install-captain 1.2.0

  # Ports the source workflow's `test` job (Tests / Operations are current /
  # Generated code is current), split in three so failing and flaky runs still
  # reach Trunk: `pytest` records pytest's exit code instead of failing,
  # `trunk-upload` uploads the JUnit files, and `test` re-fails on the saved
  # code, then runs the two --check scripts in the original order.
  - key: pytest
    use: [deps, captain]
    env:
      REQUIRE_JQ: "1"
    run: |
      mkdir -p tmp
      set +e
      captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest
      echo "$?" > tmp/pytest-exit-code

  # Uploads to Trunk Flaky Tests. TRUNK_API_TOKEN is the org-wide Trunk API
  # token (the Analytics CLI accepts no scoped key), so it lives in its own
  # `sdk-python-linear-trunk` vault -- never in `sdk-python-linear`, which holds
  # GITHUB_TOKEN and PYPI_TOKEN. Access model: locked, grants
  # `elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear:**`, `*/*`, and `:main`, approvals disabled,
  # same reasoning as `sdk-python-linear-it` (see integration-tests.yml).
  # Branch patterns do not cross `/` (measured on #192/#193), so `*/*` is what
  # lets slashed PR branches (`conductor/...`, `w-565/...`) resolve the token;
  # with only `**` and `:main` every owner PR leg fast-fails before `run:`.
  # Never add another secret to it. The `if:` is the only author gate (vault
  # grants match repo + ref, never author) and is evaluated before `env:`
  # resolves the secret, so skipped PRs (forks, other authors) never touch the
  # vault; an unresolvable secret would otherwise fail the task before `run:`.
  # cache: false + cache-key: excluded keep the token out of the content-cache
  # fingerprint and make every run actually upload. RWX is not a CI provider
  # Trunk auto-detects, so CUSTOM=true plus the job/branch/PR variables
  # attribute the run. Captain's retry command writes a separate -retry.xml
  # (see .captain/config.yml); the glob uploads both. The launcher download is
  # pinned to the same fail-closed checksum as .rwx/lint.yml's trunk-install
  # task (trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only -- no versioned URL exists),
  # the CLI reads the token from its TRUNK_API_TOKEN env default instead of a
  # --token flag so it never appears in the process list, and `< /dev/null`
  # guards against the interactive-prompt hang .rwx/lint.yml documents for
  # trunk in TTY-less CI.
  - key: trunk-upload
    use: [pytest]
    if: ${{ init.event-type != 'pull_request' || init.pr-author == 'elviskahoro' }}
    cache: false
    env:
      TRUNK_API_TOKEN:
        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-linear-trunk.secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
        cache-key: excluded
      TRUNK_ORG_SLUG: sanhedrin
      TRUNK_TEST_COLLECTION_ID: HJL9OODn
      CUSTOM: "true"
      JOB_URL: https://cloud.rwx.com/mint/elviskahoro/runs/${{ run.id }}
      BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ init.pr-number }}
      COMMIT_BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      COMMIT_SHA: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      REPO: ${{ init.repository }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      chmod 0755 "${trunk_launcher}"
      # The workspace has no .git (git/clone leaves none), so the repo
      # identity is passed explicitly (--use-uncloned-repo). Three layers keep
      # a run that uploaded nothing from going green: the CLI's own nonzero
      # exit (pipefail carries it through tee) for errored uploads, the grep
      # for its error banner in case a class of error still exits 0 under its
      # quarantining exit code, and --allow-empty-test-results=false for a
      # glob that matches no JUnit files. --pr-number is only valid when
      # non-empty (push legs set it to "").
      upload_log="$(mktemp)"
      pr_args=()
      if [ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]; then
        pr_args=(--pr-number "${PR_NUMBER}")
      fi
      "${trunk_launcher}" flakytests upload \
        --junit-paths "tmp/junit-*.xml" \
        --allow-empty-test-results=false \
        --org-url-slug "${TRUNK_ORG_SLUG}" \
        --use-uncloned-repo \
        --repo-url "${REPO}" \
        --repo-head-sha "${COMMIT_SHA}" \
        --repo-head-branch "${BRANCH}" \
        --repo-head-author-name rwx \
        --repo-head-commit-epoch "$(date +%s)" \
        "${pr_args[@]}" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee "${upload_log}"
      if grep -q "Error Encountered" "${upload_log}"; then
        echo "error: trunk upload reported an error" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}" "${upload_log}"

  # `after` is an expression, not a list: a list-form `after:` only runs the
  # task when every listed task *succeeds*, and a skipped task is not a
  # succeeded one (https://www.rwx.com/docs/after), so `after: [trunk-upload]`
  # would skip `test` on every non-owner PR leg -- a green required status
  # with no pytest run. `succeeded || skipped` keeps the upload ordered on
  # legs that run it and still gates every PR leg on the suite; a failed
  # upload (e.g. unresolvable vault) skips `test` and reddens the run there.
  - key: test
    use: [pytest]
    after: ${{ trunk-upload.succeeded || trunk-upload.skipped }}
    run: |
      code="$(cat tmp/pytest-exit-code)"
      if [ "${code}" != "0" ]; then
        echo "pytest failed (exit ${code})" >&2
        exit "${code}"
      fi
      # Fails if operations/*.graphql drifted from operations/_spec.toml.
      uv run python scripts/gen_operations.py --check
      # Fails if a generated model was hand-edited or the schema pin moved
      # without regenerating.
      uv run python scripts/codegen.py --check

  # Ports the source workflow's `lean-install` job: the wheel must build and
  # import with only its runtime deps. `use:`s [uv-install] rather than
  # [deps] to mirror the source job, which never runs uv sync -- `uv build`
  # builds in an isolated hatchling env, and the import check installs only
  # dist/*.whl into a throwaway venv.
  - key: lean-install
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      uv build
      uv venv -p 3.13 /tmp/lean
      VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/lean uv pip install dist/*.whl
      # Capture the listing before grepping it: under `set -o pipefail`,
      # `grep -q` exits on first match and uv can take SIGPIPE (141), which
      # would make the `if` false and pass the guard exactly when the leak
      # exists. Captured-then-grepped closes that fail-open window.
      lean_list="$(VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/lean uv pip list)"
      if grep -qi strawberry <<<"${lean_list}"; then
        echo "strawberry leaked into the runtime dependency tree"; exit 1
      fi
      /tmp/lean/bin/python -c "import gtm_linear; print(gtm_linear.__version__)"

  # Ports the source workflow's `schema-drift` job (originally schedule-only;
  # now runs on every trigger): network-marked tests are deselected by
  # default; this task runs them so upstream drift surfaces in CI rather
  # than in a user's traceback. Keyless by design -- no trigger needs vault
  # access to stay green: the schema test fetches Linear's public SDK schema
  # from raw.githubusercontent.com; the live-API wording check self-skips
  # without LINEAR_API_KEY (the vault key lives in `sdk-python-linear-it` and is
  # injected only by the integration-tests.yml pipeline, whose PR trigger is
  # author-gated); and
  # tests/integration's bad-key check runs keyless against api.linear.app,
  # since an invalid key must still surface AUTHENTICATION_ERROR. That last
  # call does make PR-run greenness depend on api.linear.app being reachable
  # and honoring its auth-error contract -- deliberate: it pins the exact
  # failure a user with a bad key sees.
  # cache: false is required, not cosmetic: the result depends on Linear's
  # live schema, not just this repo's files, so a cache hit would freeze the
  # drift check exactly when upstream moved. RWX caches tasks by content by
  # default and does not detect non-determinism (see
  # https://www.rwx.com/docs/caching).
  - key: schema-drift
    use: [deps, captain]
    cache: false
    run: captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest-network
```

### Gotchas visible in the reference files
- **Triggers:** `on.github` takes `pull_request`, `push` (a single item or a list of `- if:` items) and `status-checks: name:`. `on.cli`, `on.dispatch` and `on.cron` are also available. A manual run needs a `cli` entry.
- **Merge-queue branches:** the queue's `trunk-merge/**` branches are matched with `starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/')`.
- **Base image:** all files use `base: image: ubuntu:24.04` with `config: rwx/base 1.2.0`. Standard tasks are `git/clone 2.2.0`, `python/install 2.0.1`, `rwx/install-captain 1.2.0` and `github/install-cli 1.1.0`.
- **PATH:** later tasks pick up tools through `echo … >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"`.
- **Cache keys:** `filter:` applies only to the task that defines it. Anything depending on external state needs `cache: false`. Secrets use `cache-key: excluded`.
- **`after:`:** use `after: ${{ x.succeeded || x.skipped }}`. A list form silently skips gates when an upstream task is skipped.
- **Vaults:** branch globs do not cross `/`, so grants need both `**` and `*/*`. The "Allow public repositories" toggle is UI-only.
- **Repo visibility:** both reference repos are public, so `git/clone` needs no token.

### Things to confirm before porting buridan
- **Public or private:** this decides whether `git/clone` needs a `github-token`.
- **RWX GitHub App:** it must be installed on the repo, or no triggers fire.
- **Deploy:** buridan has no deploy config at all. The only trace is the old "deploy github workflow" in git history before `tests.yml` and the trunk workflows existed. Look at `e0b2329`, `ac24fb3` and `265182d` if a deploy workflow needs reviving.
- **Check names:** the three queue-required GitHub check names (`Trunk Check`, `Tests`, `Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards`) would change to `RWX: <name>` or `RWX: <file>.yml (pull request)`. Do the cutover in two stages, as in sdk-python-attio #76.
- **Impacted targets:** `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` needs `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` as a repo secret. In RWX it would become a task that reads a vault secret. Neither sibling repo has an equivalent, because neither uses graph-mode impacted targets. That workflow could stay on GitHub Actions or move to RWX.
